notable_absence.predicate: n/a - no cross-reference to native encryption at rest
notable_absence.finding: This page's entire 'Securing On-Disk Data: Encryption at Rest' section recommends ONLY 3rd-party, OS/filesystem-level transparent data encryption (LUKS, CipherTrust, Protegrity) for data, index, configuration, and password files - the exact same data classes (data/index/config/password) that manage-native-encryption-at-rest.md, this batch's own sibling page, documents Couchbase Server encrypting natively at the application layer. Neither page names, links to, or even acknowledges the other's existence anywhere in either page's text. A reader landing on this page (titled 'Manage Connections and Disks', filed as a security-recommendations page) would reasonably conclude that 3rd-party disk encryption is the ONLY way to protect data at rest on Couchbase Server, since native encryption at rest is never mentioned as an alternative or complement. This is the clearest concrete instance in the batch of the round's hypothesis-1 pattern (a genuinely separate, undocumented-as-related mechanism) turned inside out: two fully-documented, overlapping mechanisms for the same stated goal (protecting on-disk data) exist in the same directory of the same doc tree, and nothing connects them.

cross_component_finding: 'Turn on the OS-level auditing facility' (recommended for jump-server access logging) is a DIFFERENT mechanism from the promoted security:auditing concept (Couchbase Server's own per-node audit_event log, covered elsewhere in this batch's registry excerpt) - this page's auditing is OS-level (e.g. auditd), external to Couchbase Server entirely, and the page does not connect the two. Not modeled as a relation to avoid a mis-objected triple (the promoted concept's own definition explicitly warns against confusing it with unrelated audit/logging facilities); recorded here as a finding instead, per the round's own guidance not to force a relation the page's content does not actually support.
